mechanism_narrative: A strong increase in GDP growth rate indicates a growing economy, which leads to higher consumer spending and increased demand for goods and services, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of instances with strong GDP growth, or GDP growth is not significantly correlated with S&P 500 returns (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 1.5% signals a tightening monetary cycle, leading to decreased borrowing and spending, and ultimately resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances with high federal funds rates, or the federal funds rate is not significantly correlated with S&P 500 returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate, combined with high payroll employment, indicates a strong labor market, which leads to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher when both unemployment is low and payroll employment is high (p > 0.1), or the interaction term between UNRATE and PAYEMS is not significant (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production, combined with a rise in housing starts, indicates increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher when both industrial production and housing starts are increasing (p > 0.1), or the interaction term between INDPRO and HOUST is not significant (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A strong increase in retail sales indicates increased consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher when retail sales are strong (p > 0.1), or retail sales are not significantly correlated with S&P 500 returns (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate below 0.5% signals an easing monetary cycle, leading to increased borrowing and spending, and ultimately resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of instances with low federal funds rates, or the federal funds rate is not significantly correlated with S&P 500 returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A high unemployment rate, combined with low payroll employment, indicates a weak labor market, which leads to decreased consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower when both unemployment is high and payroll employment is low (p > 0.1), or the interaction term between UNRATE and PAYEMS is not significant (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production, combined with a decline in housing starts, indicates decreased economic activity and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly lower when both industrial production and housing starts are decreasing (p > 0.1), or the interaction term between INDPRO and HOUST is not significant (p > 0.1).
